lede: The sector you cannot fly to: a Crystal crewmember brings you, and the ship-unlock marker is planted on the arrival beacon before you have made a single choice. It is also the only sector whose **minimum** demand is larger than the biggest map the game can build, so it always leaves something unplaced — and always the same something, off the bottom of the table.

section_notes.HOSTILE_CRYSTAL: Six to ten beacons off five events, three of them once-only, so most of the shooting is {{CRYSTAL_FIGHT}} — which the list names three times — and {{CRYSTAL_REBEL}}. Four of the five will take a surrender; the Rebel auto-scout at {{CRYSTAL_AUTO}} has no crew to offer one. This line is settled before the neutral one is touched, so rolling the high end costs you conversations, not fights.
section_notes.BOARDERS_CRYSTAL: A prison escort rounding up intruders. Two to three Crystalline boarders, no choice offered and nothing to read — they are aboard before the text finishes. Allocated once or twice, and early enough in the queue that it always lands.
section_notes.NEUTRAL_CRYSTAL: Twelve is the ask; what it gets is the map's leftovers — at most eleven, and fewer every time a line above rolls high. This is where the sector's arithmetic is paid from. Three of the ten are a third party shooting at a Crystal ship ({{CRYSTAL_REBEL_CRYSTAL}}, {{CRYSTAL_MANTIS_CRYSTAL}}, {{CRYSTAL_PIRATE_CRYSTAL}}), where stepping in can be paid off with a Crystal weapon. {{CRYSTAL_FED_DESERTER}} is the outlier: 15–25 scrap and 1–3 fuel to a Federation ship that ran, in exchange for the map.
section_notes.ITEMS_CRYSTAL: Two beacons off a six-event list, and four of the six are the generic free weapon, free drone, refuelling station and repair station that any sector can throw at you. The two that are actually Crystalline — {{CRYSTAL_CACHE}} and {{CRYSTAL_SCRAP_EXCITED}} — are both once-only, so this is two draws from a bag where a third of the tickets are the ones worth having.
section_notes.STORE_CRYSTAL: Two to three, placed before anything else, and the only rarity table in the game that stocks the Crystal weapons — both Crystal Bursts, both Heavy Crystals, and the Lockdown Bomb that is otherwise Rock country. The only crew on sale is Crystal; every other species is set to never. Nothing in the pool can open a fourth shop, so this line is the whole of the sector's economy unless the exit hands you one.
section_notes.NOTHING_CRYSTAL: Two guaranteed dead beacons. The docked ships scatter and the station itself cloaks rather than deal with an outsider.

chain.title: Crystal Cruiser · the ship at the end of the route

steps.title: {{START_BEACON_CRYSTAL}}
steps.detail: "Here we are, my home sector." Your Crystal companion makes good on the deal and forwards the coordinates of their old ship. One option, no way to miss it — the marker is planted on arrival, before your first jump.

steps.title: The cruiser at the repair station
steps.detail: The marked beacon has no fight and no choice in it: the cruiser is shipped back to the Federation base, the station repairs **10 hull**, and you leave with a mid-tier reward and the **Crystal Vengeance** augment.

items.text: Your own Crystalline Being retunes the ship's weapons and opens {{CRYSTAL_CACHE}} with no roll at all, and turns {{CRYSTAL_CHATTY}} into free supplies.
The other clean way into the cache — one missile spent, instead of firing everything you have and mostly bouncing off.
Both pull your crewmember back out of the cache's singularity trap. Engines keep the cargo as well; the teleporter saves the person only.
Two ways through {{CRYSTAL_HUMAN_TESTS}} without putting a body on the table — the Rockman is an evolutionary cousin, the DNA bank is data they have never seen.
Worth carrying in twice over: it postpones the fleet a turn as you arrive, and at {{CRYSTAL_REQUEST}} it takes the scrap and the jump of delay with none of the chance of being caught faking it.
Only four events in the whole pool gate anything, and {{CRYSTAL_CACHE}} carries four of the seven gates by itself.

panels.title: Named things you can leave with

items.text: **Heavy Crystal Mark II** from {{CRYSTAL_HELP_DIG}} — but only by sending a crewmember down to the dig and then waiting out two full cycles.
**Crystal Lockdown Bomb** or **Crystal Burst Mark II** from {{CRYSTAL_SCRAP_EXCITED}}: pay the collector 35 scrap, then ask for payment in kind rather than taking him aboard.
A **Crystal crewmember** two ways — that same collector, or accepting the surrender at {{CRYSTAL_FIGHT}} and agreeing to take one of the survivors.
A **Human**, out of the cargo hold of the ship that was hunting them, if {{CRYSTAL_HUNTER}} surrenders.
A Crystal weapon off the cache at {{CRYSTAL_CACHE}}, and off rescuing the ship under fire at {{CRYSTAL_REBEL_CRYSTAL}}, {{CRYSTAL_MANTIS_CRYSTAL}} or {{CRYSTAL_PIRATE_CRYSTAL}}.
{{CRYSTAL_CONVOY}} repairs 8 if you stop the fight once the escort falters; {{CRYSTAL_CHATTY}} repairs 6 on one of the three ways the conversation can go.

Three events can cost a crewmember and all three are your own choice: the singularity in {{CRYSTAL_CACHE}}, the dig at {{CRYSTAL_HELP_DIG}}, and letting the scientists at {{CRYSTAL_HUMAN_TESTS}} run their tests.
Three events put Crystalline crew on your ship — two to three at {{BOARDERS_CRYSTAL}} and again if the cache's owners are home, one or two at {{CRYSTAL_REQUEST}} if they catch you lying.

{{CRYSTAL_HELP_DIG}} advances the Rebel fleet a jump for every cycle you wait, and the Heavy Crystal is behind two of them. {{CRYSTAL_REBEL_CRYSTAL}} advances it one if you shoot the Crystal ship rather than the Rebel.
The cache escape that saves both the crewmember and the cargo detonates **your entire fuel reserve** to do it. Advanced Engines do the same job for nothing.

{{CRYSTAL_HUMAN_TESTS}} can answer a flat no by undocking a warship that will not accept surrender. {{CRYSTAL_HELP_DIG}} is safe to decline outright — it only turns hostile if you promise help and then pull your crewmember back out.

No event in the sector sets an environment — no asteroid field, no sun, no pulsar anywhere in the pool — so the only hazard here is the one the Rebels bring with a beacon they have taken, and Long-Ranged Scanners have nothing to warn you about. There is no cloud to duck into either, so the universal way of halving the fleet's advance is off the table.
